flawed_step: Line 0019 claims that, in an arbitrary model satisfying φ1∧φ2, c∈C iff ∃z P(z,z). Arbitrary interpretations can collapse distinct encoded strings to the same domain element, so the reverse implication fails.
counterexample: Let c consist of the single tile (0,1), which has no nonempty PCP solution because 0^n≠1^n for every n≥1. Take the one-element model A={a}, with e=a, f0(a)=f1(a)=a, and P={(a,a)}. Then φ1 holds since P(f0(e),f1(e))=P(a,a). Formula φ2 holds because its only required instance is P(a,a)→P(a,a). Also φ3 holds since P(a,a). Thus ∃z P(z,z) holds although c∉C, directly contradicting line 0019.
assessment_summary: The asserted biconditional confuses equality of interpreted domain elements with equality of the original strings. The interpretation map need not be injective in an arbitrary model.
